p:cNvPr.descr: This diagram illustrates how G proteins cycle between GDP-bound (off) and GTP-bound (on) phases of the GTPase switch. The GTPase switch is illustrated as a yellow rectangular plane with V-shaped yellow tails on the inside and two parallel horizontal blue beaded rows about a centimeter apart, bordering the yellow plane. There are three large structures, two GPCR and one adenylyl cyclase segmented evenly across. The GTPase switch comprises four phases. In the first phase, Gs, represented by two green ovals with two valves sticking out at the top into the yellow plane, is bound to GDP, represented by a gray horizontal oval, and to GPCR, represented by a tan-orangish boulder-like structure with folds of pink and red ribbons in it. The Gs structure is also linked to a green ovular structure labeled beta, and Gs has two tails labeled gamma. This is step 1, which is described as "Gs with GDP bound is turned off; it cannot activate adenylyl cyclase." To the right of this is an arrow that points right to the same structures, except this time, there is a small brown boulder looped into the ribbons in the GPCR structure. On the top left, there's a similar boulder from which an arrow points away to the bottom right to the boulder inside the GPCR. To the right of the Gs and its constituent pieces is an arrow pointing right that has an arrow curving into it from the top, with an orange oval labeled GTP coming into it, and an arrow curving down away from it on the bottom, pointing to the GDP shape. This is step 2, described as "Contact of Gs with hormonereceptor complex causes displacement of bound GDP by GTP." To the right of these arrows is a similar green structure; this time, about half the size of the previous ones. The GTP is bonded at the center of it, and it is labeled, alpha. This green structure has hairlike extensions all around it, and it is bonded to a blue toothlike structure on the yellow and blue plane, labeled Adenylyl cyclase. It too has hairlike extensions all around it. This is step 3, described as, "Gs with GTP bound dissociates into alpha and beta-gamma subunits. Gs alpha-GTP is turned on; it can activate adenylyl cyclase." To the bottom of these structures, a two-headed arrow curves right to Pi, and left to a similar green structure that has alpha on it and the gray oval, GDP, on it. To the left of this is a curved arrow upward that points to the first set of structures described. A second arrow curves into the arrow from the second set of structures. This is step 4, described as, "GTP bound to Gs alpha is hydrolyzed by the protein's intrinsic GTPase; Gs alpha thereby turns itself off. The inactive alpha subunit reassociates with the beta gamma subunit."
